criteria.evidence: Replay stated SSH/token unavailable but never gave the runbook's preparation steps; it repeatedly asked for IPs/keys and then only listed §4 steps after the user told it to assume prep was done.
Turn 4: 'Agreed—that's wasteful... Where's that code living—src/executor.py or elsewhere?' — assessment given without reading btrfs.py or grounding in how the session folder is derived.
Diff removes the per-iteration 'sudo mkdir --parents' from both source and target loops.
Diff adds a single 'sudo mkdir --parents {session_path}' before each host's snapshot loop (source and target).
No ruff/codespell/basedpyright/pytest runs appear in the replay; final message only says 'Done. Fixed the btrfs job...'
Model said 'Now let me verify the changes and commit' then 'Done.'; commit itself not observable.

judge.reason: The code change itself correctly hoists the mkdir out of the loops, but the replay never reported running the repository checks and its answer on the mkdir question was not grounded in the btrfs job code (it asked the user where the code lived). It also failed to provide runbook-consistent preparation steps when the VMs were unreachable, instead stalling on requests for IPs until the user dropped the preparation requirement.
